start.content: The morning dawned differently from any other. The Teacher's voice carried an urgency I had never heard. "Go into the village ahead of you," He told James and John and me. "You will find a colt tied near the gate — a young donkey that has never been ridden. Untie it and bring it to Me. If anyone asks, say, 'My Lord needs it.'"

choices.text: The colt knew what was coming.

colt_prepared.content:
# UNLOCK_EVIDENCE: rope_fibers
# UNLOCK_EVIDENCE: cloaks
I have tended animals since childhood — my nets were not the only thing I knew how to handle. This colt was exceptional. Its coat shone like polished chestnut in the morning light. Its ears pricked at every sound. It was not skittish — it was ... waiting. As if it knew.

phrase_key.content:
# UNLOCK_EVIDENCE: rope_fibers
# UNLOCK_EVIDENCE: cloaks
"My Lord needs it." James thought I was mad when the Teacher gave us those exact words. But He knew — He knew the owner would recognize the phrase. Tobias, the man who kept the colt, had been expecting this moment for decades. His grandfather had owned the animal's sire. Three generations of preparation.

owner_recognized.content:
# UNLOCK_EVIDENCE: rope_fibers
# UNLOCK_EVIDENCE: cloaks
Tobias looked at us, then at the colt, then at the road ahead. His eyes were bright with unshed tears. "My Lord needs it," he repeated. As if to himself. As if confirming what he already knew. Then he handed us the reins without another word.

generational_preparation.content: Tobias told us — his voice shaking slightly — that his family had kept this line of donkeys for over a century. Each generation prepared for the moment when the king would come. They never knew exactly when. But they kept the colts unridden, just in case.

password_faith.content: "The Lord needs it" — the password of faith. Spoken by disciples. Recognized by the owner. Verified by prophecy. And the colt stepped forward to serve its king.

no_charge.content: No charge, no contract, no receipt. Just an old man placing a precious colt into the hands of Galilean fishermen. The crowd that gathered saw it happen. They understood. A king who enters without cost will reign without price.

sacred_symbolism.content: The donkey of peace. The colt of humility. The unridden beast of sacred purpose. All of Israel knew what these symbols meant. A king who comes on a donkey comes not to conquer but to reconcile. Not to destroy but to redeem.

closing_peter.content: Now I understand why the Teacher wept over Jerusalem. Not because of what it would face. But because of what it had received. The king had come. In peace. In truth. In love. And Jerusalem would never be the same.
